--- a/minbpe/_rare.py
+++ b/minbpe/_rare.py
@@ -0,0 +1,95 @@
+"""
+Helpers of minbpe.base that are rarely needed (very long inputs to
+apply_merges, pretty printing of tokens). They live in their own module so
+that importing the package does not have to load them.
+"""
+from heapq import heapify, heappop, heappush
+
+
+def _apply_merges_heap(ids, merges):
+    """
+    Same result as apply_merges, for long sequences: a doubly linked list over
+    the original positions plus a heap of (rank, position) entries for every
+    mergeable adjacent pair. Entries are validated lazily when popped (a pair
+    whose tokens changed is recomputed), and each round pops all entries of the
+    minimal rank in position order, i.e. sequence order. The first valid one
+    picks the pair (same as the first-seen minimal pair); its occurrences are
+    merged left to right, skipping overlaps, exactly like merge().
+    """
+    merges_get = merges.get
+    n = len(ids)
+    val = list(ids)
+    nxt = list(range(1, n + 1)) # n means "no next"
+    prv = list(range(-1, n - 1)) # -1 means "no previous"
+    heap = [(r, i) for i, r in enumerate(map(merges_get, zip(val, val[1:])))
+            if r is not None]
+    heapify(heap)
+    while heap:
+        r = heap[0][0]
+        pair = None
+        last = -1
+        merged = []
+        rest = []
+        while heap and heap[0][0] == r:
+            p = heappop(heap)[1]
+            if p == last:
+                continue # duplicate entry (pops come out in position order)
+            last = p
+            v = val[p]
+            if v is None:
+                continue # position was merged away
+            q = nxt[p]
+            if q == n:
+                continue
+            pr = (v, val[q])
+            if merges_get(pr) != r:
+                continue # stale entry
+            if pair is None:
+                pair = pr
+            elif pr != pair:
+                rest.append(p) # another pair with the same rank: later round
+                continue
+            val[p] = r
+            val[q] = None
+            q2 = nxt[q]
+            nxt[p] = q2
+            if q2 < n:
+                prv[q2] = p
+            merged.append(p)
+        for p in rest:
+            heappush(heap, (r, p))
+        for p in merged:
+            a = prv[p]
+            if a >= 0:
+                rk = merges_get((val[a], r))
+                if rk is not None:
+                    heappush(heap, (rk, a))
+            b = nxt[p]
+            if b < n:
+                rk = merges_get((r, val[b]))
+                if rk is not None:
+                    heappush(heap, (rk, p))
+    return [v for v in val if v is not None]
+
+
+def replace_control_characters(s: str) -> str:
+    # we don't want to print control characters
+    # which distort the output (e.g. \n or much worse)
+    # https://stackoverflow.com/questions/4324790/removing-control-characters-from-a-string-in-python/19016117#19016117
+    # http://www.unicode.org/reports/tr44/#GC_Values_Table
+    import unicodedata
+    chars = []
+    for ch in s:
+        if unicodedata.category(ch)[0] != "C":
+            chars.append(ch) # this character is ok
+        else:
+            chars.append(f"\\u{ord(ch):04x}") # escape
+    return "".join(chars)
+
+
+def render_token(t: bytes) -> str:
+    # pretty print a token, escaping control characters
+    s = t.decode('utf-8', errors='replace')
+    s = replace_control_characters(s)
+    return s
+

I also searched for import and minbpe. usages, which turned up 60 matching lines, to see how the modules depend on each other. Then I wrote a new file, minbpe/_rare.py, with 95 lines.

I never ran a sandbox evaluation. Nothing I wrote has been measured, and the session stopped without a candidate, so there is no result to report. The new file is not wired into anything I checked, and I have no evidence it changes the bench at all.

What I now believe is limited to what the reading showed. The tokenizer logic is spread across base.py, basic.py and regex.py, with gpt4.py layered on top. Any change has to respect how those modules import each other, and the bench in lineage_bench.py is what matters.

Next time I should start by running the bench unchanged to get a baseline. Then I should decide whether _rare.py is worth hooking in, and evaluate it in the sandbox before writing more code.
